tasks.description: Build the main game loop: pick a word, loop until won or out of tries. Ask for a guess each iteration and update the display.
tasks.hint:
`while not is_won(word, guessed) and tries_left > 0:`
Inside: show the blank display, ask for input, call `check_guess()`.
Only decrement `tries_left` when the guess is WRONG (not in the word).
tasks.walkthrough:
The loop keeps going while the word isn't complete and there are tries left.
Each pass shows the current blanks, reads a letter, records it, and adds it to the wrong list if it isn't in the word.
The tries left are calculated from the wrong list each time.

tasks.description: Handle the case where the user guesses a letter they already guessed — print 'Already guessed that!' and don't count it as a try.
tasks.hint:
At the top of each loop iteration: `if guess in guessed: print('Already guessed that!'); continue`
`continue` skips the rest of the loop body — no try lost, no update.
Only process and count guesses that are NEW.
tasks.walkthrough:
The repeat check happens before the guess is added to anything.
`continue` jumps back to the loop condition, so a repeated letter costs no tries and changes nothing.

tasks.description: At the end of the game: if the player won, print 'You won! The word was: {word}'. If they lost, print 'Game over! The word was: {word}'.
tasks.hint:
After the while loop, check which condition ended it.
`if is_won(word, guessed): print(f'You won! ...')` else the loss message.
Always reveal the word at the end — even on a win.
tasks.walkthrough:
When the loop stops, `is_won` tells you why: either every letter was found, or the tries ran out.
The word is revealed in both messages so the player always learns the answer.

tasks.description: Add input validation: only accept single letters. If the user enters more than one character or a non-letter, ask again.
tasks.hint:
After getting input: `if len(guess) != 1 or not guess.isalpha(): print('Enter a single letter!'); continue`
`.isalpha()` returns True only for alphabetic characters.
This prevents crashes from numbers, spaces, or empty input.
tasks.walkthrough:
The validation check comes first so that bad input never reaches the game logic.
`len(guess) != 1` rejects empty input and multi-letter strings; `not guess.isalpha()` rejects digits and symbols.

tasks.description: Add a visual lives counter. Print a row of hearts ❤ for remaining tries: '❤ ❤ ❤ _ _' (hearts for tries left, _ for lost).
tasks.hint:
Calculate tries lost: `lost = max_tries - tries_left`
Build the display: `'❤ ' * tries_left + '_ ' * lost`
Strip the trailing space: `.strip()` or use `join()`.
tasks.walkthrough:
`lives()` builds the bar from two repeated strings: one heart per try left, one underscore per try lost.
`.strip()` removes the trailing space so the line ends cleanly.
It's printed at the top of every round, so the player always sees where they stand.

lesson.intro:
Today the pieces become a game. The heart of it is one loop: while the player
hasn't won and still has tries, show the word, ask for a letter, update. Then a
few improvements that make it feel finished: rejecting repeats, validating
input, and a lives display.

sections.heading: The main loop
sections.body:
The loop condition combines two checks with `and`. Inside, the same three
steps every time. A wrong guess adds to the wrong list; a right one doesn't
cost anything.

sections.heading: Repeated and invalid guesses
sections.body:
Check the input before doing anything with it. `continue` sends the loop
straight back to the top without counting the guess. `.isalpha()` is True
only for letters.
sections.output:
'a': already guessed
'7': enter a single letter
'ab': enter a single letter
'b': ok

sections.heading: Win or lose message
sections.body:
After the loop, one of the two conditions must have failed. Check `is_won`
to know which. Reveal the word either way.
sections.output: You won! The word was: hi

sections.heading: A lives display
sections.body:
Repeating a string with `*` is a quick way to draw a bar. Hearts for tries
left, underscores for tries lost, then strip the trailing space.
sections.code:

lost = max_tries - tries_left

watch_out: Counting a repeated guess as a wrong one. Check `guess in guessed` before anything else.
Lowercasing the input. If the word is lowercase, `guess.lower()` avoids a mismatch on capital letters.
Reducing the tries on every guess instead of only wrong ones.
In this app, list all your guesses in the input box, one per line, before you run.
